🎨 ComfyUI Smart Drawing
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
/draw <description>  draw from one sentence
  inline options: 16:9 / --size 1024x1536 / --seed 42
                  --steps 30 / --cfg 6 / --lora name:0.8
                  --model keyword / --batch 2 / --negative "..."
            --llm force AI prompt rewrite / --no-llm skip it this time
/i2i      repaint from a photo (--denoise controls strength)
/outpaint extend the canvas (--left/--right/--top/--bottom px)
/video    text-to-video (--seconds / --fps / --length)
/i2v      animate a photo (send two photos = first → last frame)
/prompt   reverse-engineer a prompt from an image (--draw to draw at once)
/models   list available models
/templates list workflow templates (custom ones supported)
/status   ComfyUI connection and queue
/cancel   cancel your queued/running job (admin: /cancel all)
/audit     view audit log (admin, optional --user ID)
/inspect   model inspection: duplicates / misplaced / unused (admin)
/health    environment health check: flags / memory / template deps (admin)
/stats    usage statistics
/refresh-models  re-read the model list (admin)
/help     show this help

llm.optimize_system:
You are a ComfyUI prompt engineer. Rewrite the user's description into a high-quality English prompt and pick the most suitable model from the given list.
Rules:
1. Only use model filenames that appear **verbatim** in the list; never invent one or change case/paths.
2. If unsure whether a LoRA fits, leave the lora field as an empty string.
3. Write the prompt as comma-separated English tags, with no explanatory prose.
4. The negative prompt must include the usual hand/anatomy guards, at least: bad hands, extra fingers, fewer fingers, fused fingers, extra digits, missing fingers, mutated hands, malformed limbs, bad anatomy.
5. Describe the hands explicitly in the positive prompt (e.g. hands on hips, holding a cup, arms crossed) so the model has a concrete action to draw — this beats fixing it afterwards.
6. Output exactly one JSON object, no markdown fences, no other text.
Format: {"positive": "...", "negative": "...", "checkpoint": "...", "lora": "...", "lora_strength": 1.0, "vae": "", "width": 0, "height": 0}
llm.reverse_system:
You reverse-engineer prompts for anime/illustration images. Look at the image and output English Danbooru-style tags usable in Stable Diffusion.
Rules:
1. Only describe what is **actually visible**; never invent unclear clothing patterns or accessories.
2. Order the positive tags like this: subject count (solo / 1girl / 2girls) → appearance (hair colour and style, eye colour) → clothing → action and **hand state** (e.g. hands on hips, holding a cup) → camera and framing (from above, upper body, full body) → background → lighting and mood → art style (anime style, watercolour, ...).
3. Give 8~15 common defect guards in negative (including hands/anatomy: bad hands, extra fingers, fused fingers, missing fingers, malformed limbs).
4. Write summary as one short sentence.
5. Output exactly one JSON object, no markdown fences, no other text.
Format: {"positive": "...", "negative": "...", "summary": "..."}
llm.reverse_user: Look at this image and reverse-engineer a prompt usable in Stable Diffusion.{hint}
llm.video_system:
You are an AI video prompt engineer. Rewrite the user's description as a **video** prompt, not image tags.
Rules:
1. Always describe **motion**: who does what and how it changes (e.g. "slowly turns her head").
2. Give exactly **one** camera move: static / slow push-in / lateral pan / slight handheld.
3. Cover subject + outfit, then environment, then lighting/mood - one or two clauses each, no tag spam.
4. **Keep the user's language**: if the user writes Chinese, answer in Chinese (Wan understands Chinese natively).
5. Length: 25-50 English words (or 40-80 Chinese characters).
6. Never use words like "static", "still", "video", "frame", and never mention models or settings.
7. Output JSON: {"positive": "...", "negative": "one generic negative phrase or empty string"}; negative should only cover quality/structure (watermark, deformed limbs, blurry).
Output JSON only, no explanation.

ui.text.001: ComfyUI address reachable from the machine running AstrBot.
ui.text.002: Ask ComfyUI to free VRAM/RAM before switching model families (video <-> SDXL). On 16G machines this avoids the os error 1455 crash. On by default.
ui.text.003: With several ComfyUI instances jobs go to the least busy one; a failing backend is temporarily skipped. Leave empty for a single backend.
ui.text.004: Limit concurrent generations; extra requests queue with their position shown.
ui.text.005: Read straight from ComfyUI's model folders. Only models listed here are used.
ui.text.006: Loaded automatically when you open this tab.
ui.text.007: Use an LLM to rewrite the description and pick a checkpoint/LoRA from the real model list.
ui.text.008: When off, your text is used as-is with the first available checkpoint; no LLM needed.
ui.text.009: When on, /video and /i2v first rewrite your text into a **video prompt**: it adds the motion (slowly turning her head, gentle swaying), one camera move (static / push-in / pan) and the lighting mood, while keeping your language (Chinese stays Chinese - Wan understands it). Unlike images (English tags), video wants natural-language action. The model comes from the "default t2v / i2v model" fields below - the AI only rewrites the prompt. Override per message with --llm / --no-llm.
ui.text.010: /reverse needs a vision-capable model. Without it AstrBot replaces the image with "[Image]" and the model invents content.
ui.text.011: Add a vision model (qwen-vl-max, glm-4v, gpt-4o, ...) in AstrBot's providers and put its ID here.
ui.text.012: When a base URL is set, the provider above is ignored.
ui.text.013: Test another model without editing config: /reverse --provider <id>. /status shows the active vision model.
ui.text.014: Resolution, CFG and sampler are adapted to the checkpoint architecture (SD1.5 / SDXL / Pony / Flux).
ui.text.015: When off, the values below are only fallbacks for unknown architectures.
ui.text.016: Quality tags are added for SD1.5 / Pony, not for SDXL / Flux.
ui.text.018: Send an image with a description to redraw it; /img2img works with just an image too.
ui.text.019: When off, attached images fall back to text-to-image; /img2img still works explicitly.
ui.text.020: Denoise: 0.3 touches details, 0.6 (default) changes style, 0.8+ almost redraws. Size follows the source aspect ratio, aligned to 8.
ui.text.021: Generate small, then upscale and redraw. Best for hands/faces/details; roughly doubles the time.
ui.text.022: Every /draw runs an extra upscale pass.
ui.text.024: When on, users may pass --hires 1.5 or --hires 0; when off your settings always win.
ui.text.025: Final size = original x factor, aligned to 8. On 8GB cards keep the factor at or below 1.5.
ui.text.026: Generate short videos with /video; needs video models and nodes installed in ComfyUI (e.g. Wan 2.x).
ui.text.027: The tier caps resolution / frames / steps: low 480p, <=97 frames, <=12 steps; mid 720p, <=121, <=30; high 720p, <=161, <=50. Auto detects VRAM and drops a tier below 20G RAM. On low/mid tiers an unnamed model prefers files containing turbo / lightning / distill / schnell (measured: Turbo 4 steps = 74 s vs 20 steps = 281 s). Filling a model name above always wins.
ui.text.028: When off, only the local file path is sent (for platforms that cannot play video).
ui.text.029: Images are pruned by age and count to protect disk space.
ui.text.030: Mention the requester when drawing in a group.
ui.text.031: Show template, checkpoint, size, seed and time for reproducibility.
ui.text.032: Live "step n / total" over ComfyUI's WebSocket; falls back to polling without affecting the result.
ui.text.033: Upload an image, paint over what should change (red), write a description, then run inpaint. The mask is built in your browser only.
ui.text.034: No result yet. Upload an image, paint a mask, then run inpaint.
ui.text.035: Admin rights come from AstrBot itself; here you only maintain lists and limits.
ui.text.036: When off, admins are limited too (the blacklist always wins).
ui.text.037: Record every generation (who/when/purpose/model/time/first 60 chars) and content-filter blocks; admins read it with /audit.
ui.text.038: Feature names: t2i / i2i / outpaint / inpaint / t2v / i2v / reverse_prompt, or all / none. Priority: user > group > default > the feature switches under Advanced.
ui.text.039: Prompts matching the word list are blocked; both the raw text and the AI-rewritten prompt are checked.
ui.text.040: Off by default (silent, like feature switches); when on the user gets a short notice.
ui.text.041: This language drives both the plugin page and chat messages.
ui.text.042: Only text-to-image is on by default. Disabled features are silently ignored (no reply) and cost no VRAM; the LLM tool obeys this too.
ui.text.044: Image-to-image uses more VRAM and can edit others' images; enable deliberately.
ui.text.045: Extend the canvas outwards; VRAM grows with the margin.
ui.text.046: Redraw a painted region; the Inpaint tab reports it as unavailable when off.
ui.text.047: Heaviest feature: 74-281 s per clip on an 8G card.
ui.text.048: Animate a still (two images = first/last frame). Also VRAM heavy.
ui.text.049: Not generation strictly speaking, but it calls a vision model, so it has a switch too.
ui.text.050: Let the chat model call the drawing tool when the user says "draw me ...".
ui.text.051: Requires tool calling; the drawing tool is exposed to the chat model when on.
ui.text.053: Model inspection (duplicates / misplaced / unused) plus an environment health check (flags / memory / template dependencies).
ui.text.054: Click "Run inspection" to build the report.
ui.text.055: Built-in templates are picked by architecture; drop API-format JSON into the custom folder to add one.
ui.text.056: Generation counts, model usage and a gallery.
